questions.q: What does the Driver actually send to Executors?
options: The entire dataset, copied to every Executor
Serialized instructions describing the computation to run — not the raw data itself
A full copy of the Driver's memory
Nothing — Executors work independently with no communication from the Driver
questions.explain: This pairs with Lesson 29's data locality — the instructions travel; the data mostly stays where it already is.

questions.q: Why don't Executors send their full results back to the Driver by default?
options: The Driver never needs any information about job completion
Sending results back is always required for every single operation
Executors are physically incapable of sending any data back
Doing so for a large dataset would recreate the exact memory problem Spark exists to avoid
questions.explain: Instead, most operations write results to storage directly and just report completion back to the Driver.

questions.q: When do Executors send actual values back to the Driver?
options: Never, under any circumstances
Only when the Cluster Manager specifically requests it
For every single operation, regardless of size
For a genuinely small result the Driver explicitly asked for, like count() or collect() on a small DataFrame
questions.explain: This distinction previews Lesson 35's transformations (stay distributed) versus actions (return something to the Driver).

questions.q: Why is the fact that the Driver builds an entire plan before execution significant?
options: It prevents Spark from ever using multiple Executors
It has no real benefit and only adds unnecessary delay
It means the plan can never be changed once built
It lets Spark look at everything at once and optimize the whole plan, rather than running each operation immediately like Pandas does
questions.explain: This is exactly why Lesson 34's lazy evaluation is possible — the plan-first approach enables whole-plan optimization.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, what would calling .count() on a 500-million-row DataFrame actually send back to the Driver?
options: All 500 million rows, copied in full
Exactly half of the rows, chosen randomly
A single small number (the count), not the 500 million rows themselves
Nothing at all — count() cannot be executed
questions.explain: count() is an action requesting a small, specific result — not the full dataset.
